newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer in active trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer in active trade.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended firmer in active trade on Wednesday but dealers were wary of possible further U.S. selling.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6875/82 and 68.01 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6869/76 and 67.81 at the opening.
"The main question is: will the United States attack it again? Every night for the last few the New Yorkers have sold it, and they've sold it in volume," a Wellington dealer said.
However, he said it was encouraging that, for the first time in some days, the Kiwi was finishing on its highs, and that could portend a move back upwards.
"The market has become extraordinarily bearish on the back of very little," the dealer said, adding recent weakness may have been a false downward move due to technical selling.

Kiwi briefly moved downwards with the Australian dollar on subdued Australian inflation data which was seen as providing scope for another interest rate cut, but both subsequently recovered to previous levels.
An Auckland dealer said there was interest to buy Kiwi below US$0.6850, and the general perception was that U.S. dollar strength would cap the currency initially around 0.6900.
